item.title: Crip Mac Mall Meet-And-Greet Marred By Stabbing & Arrest
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Crip Mac's Santa Rosa meet-and-greet is followed by a stabbing investigation, a suspect's surrender and a call for witnesses.
item.content:encoded:
Crip Mac‘s mall appearance in Santa Rosa is drawing attention after a stabbing left a man seriously injured. Local reports connect the rapper’s meet-and-greet to the location of Sunday’s violence.

The Los Angeles rapper was signing autographs and taking photos at the clothing store when the fight broke out, according to the San Francisco Chronicle, which identified him through social media posts.

Police described the event in their release without naming the entertainer.

Officers arrived around 1:10 p.m. November 8 and found a man stabbed in the back near the food court. “The victim was transported to a local hospital for treatment of serious injuries and is expected to survive,” police said in their official release.

Police identified the suspect as 26-year-old Santa Rosa resident Marcus Temple, who turned himself in around 4:06 p.m. He was booked on suspicion of assault with a deadly weapon, and the release doesn’t accuse Crip Mac of participating in the attack.

Investigators say several people fought near the store hosting the appearance, then many participants and witnesses left before officers arrived. Mall security supplied surveillance footage, and the department’s Gang Crimes Team took over the investigation.

Crip Mac’s appearances have extended beyond music and online interviews into the celebrity fight circuit. He was also on a September Smack Fighting Championships card, as AllHipHop previously reported while covering Treach’s involvement with the promotion.

Detectives believe additional bystanders recorded Sunday’s incident on their phones and want those people to come forward.

Officers searching the mall didn’t recover the knife, according to the department’s account.

Anyone with information can contact the Gang Crimes Team at 707-543-4021.

item.title: Cardi B Apologizes To Jamaica’s Government & Blames Concert Promoter
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cardi B takes her Jamaica booking battle back to the promoter, saying his messages put government officials in the mix.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B apologized to Jamaica’s government while accusing concert promoter Ryan Burke of dragging officials into her canceled BZR WKND booking dispute.

She says his communications, not any direct conversation with the government, were behind her earlier claims.

“I want to apologise to the Government of Jamaica because I feel like motherf*****s was putting your name in the finesse,” Cardi B said on Instagram Live.

The newspaper reported that she accused Burke of telling her team the government had invested in the event.

Cardi B said she had emails and messages backing up her account and challenged Burke to dispute it. She also acknowledged she could not verify whether his alleged claim of government investment was true.

Her apology followed a statement from Jamaica’s Ministry of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, which denied paying or promising money toward her appearance in a statement to The Jamaica Star

Officials characterized the booking as a private arrangement between the artist’s representatives and the promoter.

BZR organizers have separately insisted the festival used private funding and that no government assistance was received or promised.

The apology does not settle the separate fight over how much Cardi B received and why the show fell apart.

Burke previously claimed she had been paid the full $2.5 million performance fee, while she said she received a $1 million deposit.

Production expenses are another point of contention. Cardi B has maintained that money needed to stage the performance arrived too late and that she returned funds sent after the cancellation.

The concert was originally promoted for October 18 at Kingston’s National Stadium, putting one of rap’s biggest stars at the center of a major Jamaican event.

Its collapse has since produced competing public accounts of the deal, refund questions and threats of legal action.

Burke has said he intends to pursue legal action, while Cardi B has threatened a countersuit. Burke also said ticket refunds had started and described seeking the return of performance money after the new date began looking doubtful.

When her withdrawal was announced, Cardi B’s representatives directed ticket holders to the promoters for event information.

Her team also urged people to watch her official channels for future performance announcements.

Burke says organizers are still working toward a December 20 event.

item.title: Ice Cube Puts Story Before Cameos For Last Friday
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ice Cube sets a limit on Last Friday reunions as Mike Epps gets calls from people hoping to return to the franchise.
item.content:encoded:
Ice Cube isn’t handing out “Last Friday” appearances just because somebody wants another turn on the block. He’s making the story the deciding factor as familiar faces look for a place in the long-awaited fourth movie.

During a Club Shay Shay conversation released November 11, Cube explained that returning characters need a reason to be there. Mike Epps described getting calls from people interested in coming back, including someone who had previously worked as an extra.

“We can’t just be throwing people in the movie just because people want to see them,” Cube told Shannon Sharpe.

He said the choices have to work with the plot, then pointed to the franchise’s move away from its original neighborhood.

Cube recalled leaving characters behind when the action shifted to Rancho Cucamonga. That change brought a different setting and different people, rather than putting the entire original cast into another location.

He explained that the focus was on how the characters fit together, not simply bringing everyone back. “It just got to make sense,” Cube told Shannon Sharpe.

The conversation arrives after Lawrence Lamont joined Last Friday as director, bringing experience with another neighborhood comedy. Lamont directed Keke Palmer and SZA in “One Of Them Days,” about two friends scrambling to save their home after their rent money disappears.

He’s also worked with rappers on the music-video side, including Big Sean and J. Cole. His television credits include “Rap Sh!t,” giving him another connection to stories built around Hip-Hop and the people trying to make a living around it.

The “Friday” series began in 1995 with Cube and Chris Tucker, with F. Gary Gray directing the original. Epps later joined as Day-Day, and the series hasn’t added another movie since “Friday After Next” arrived in 2002. The first film introduced Tucker’s Smokey alongside Cube’s Craig, while John Witherspoon played Craig’s father and became another fixture of the series.

The new production has California tax-credit support, with New Line’s “Last Friday” included in the state’s October 7 awards. Cube serves as the movie’s star, writer and producer for its return to Southern California.

The Southern California production plans to employ more than 180 local cast and crew members.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Takes Tha Dogg House To Spain With Members-Only Club
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Snoop Dogg expands Tha Dogg House to Barcelona with a members-only club after building his cannabis presence in Amsterdam.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg is taking Tha Dogg House into Spain with a members-only cannabis club that adds another country to his European business.

The Barcelona expansion follows two locations in Amsterdam, giving the brand its third European storefront.

Snoop described the project as a neighborhood gathering place built around music and company, connecting it to the reception he’s received across Europe.

“From Paris to Milan to Amsterdam, Europe has shown me nothing but love,” Snoop said in an announcement.

The new club brings that international presence into a business shaped around Spain’s cannabis social-club model.

Membership will be restricted to adults 18 and older, with no sales to nonmembers. The announcement also rules out consumption outside the premises and says the operation will follow applicable Spanish and Catalan requirements.

Snoop’s cannabis ventures already reach well beyond putting his face on a package.

AllHipHop previously covered his first Los Angeles dispensary opening in July 2024, when he paired the launch with a Tupac Shakur-themed collection from Death Row Cannabis.

That store opened near Los Angeles International Airport under the S.W.E.D. name, short for Smoke Weed Every Day. Death Row Cannabis had launched in 2023, adding a cannabis operation to a name already central to his recording career.

His first Amsterdam coffeeshop followed that same summer, with an August 1, 2024 opening date announced by Death Row Records Cannabis.

The two-level space combined a retail floor with a basement lounge, making the setting part of the pitch alongside the products.

The original Amsterdam announcement described graffiti, Snoop-related artwork and a giant golden Doberman statue among the interior touches.

Those details show how his stores have used recognizable pieces of his persona to build spaces around the brand.

The expansion also follows a U.S. branding setback AllHipHop reported in March. Federal trademark officials rejected his bid to register Smoke Weed Everyday, citing both marijuana’s federal illegality and the phrase’s widespread use as a message rather than a brand.

The Barcelona club’s announced location is Carrer de Peracamps, 9, in the city.

item.title: iHeartMedia Denies Podcast Sale After The Breakfast Club Expands
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: iHeartMedia pushes back on a podcast selloff report as The Breakfast Club's parent puts up $174 million in quarterly sales.
item.content:encoded:
iHeartMedia says its podcast empire isn’t for sale as questions swirl around the company behind some of Hip-Hop’s biggest conversations.

That business includes The Breakfast Club and its partnership with Charlamagne Tha God‘s Black Effect network.

A company spokesperson rejected the sale speculation in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter on Wednesday.

The response followed a Bloomberg report that iHeart had discussed potentially selling some or all of its podcast operation.

“While we don’t generally comment on rumors or speculation, I can tell you that we have no plan to sell our podcasting business,” the spokesperson said.

The company also said it intends to keep investing in podcasts, including their video reach.

The financial backdrop explains why that division is drawing attention right now.

Podcast revenue reached $174 million last quarter, rising 24.6 percent from a year earlier, while companywide adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization fell 17 percent to $170.5 million.

For Hip-Hop listeners, the business stretches well beyond a morning radio broadcast.

The Breakfast Club expanded onto Netflix’s daily live schedule in June with Charlamagne, Loren Loroso, DJ Envy and Jess Hilarious at the center of the show.

The show began in 2010 and originates from New York’s Power 105.1, carrying the same interviews across radio, on-demand audio and a subscription video service rather than relying on a single outlet.

That arrangement gave Netflix viewers nearly three continuous hours of programming, including bonus material during radio commercial breaks. iHeart retained the audio rights, while the radio version continued through Premiere Networks and more than 100 stations nationwide.

The company’s Black Effect partnership also connects it to N.O.R.E. and DJ EFN’s growing podcast operation. Their Drink Champs Podcast Network launched with Black Effect in 2025, extending the hosts’ work into a wider slate of shows.

Memphis Bleek’s ROC Solid became that network’s first series, with Ja Rule appearing in the debut episode. Distribution through iHeartPodcasts put those conversations on the iHeartRadio app and other podcast platforms, adding another route for rappers to build media businesses.

iHeart plans to report podcasting separately from its Digital Audio Group beginning in 2027.

item.title: The Roots Set Fourth Hollywood Bowl Picnic With Tickets On Sale This Week
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The Roots put Los Angeles on the summer calendar again as their 2027 Bowl date arrives ahead of this week's ticket rush.
item.content:encoded:
The Roots are giving Los Angeles a reason to plan next summer before this week’s ticket sale even opens. A Roots Picnic Experience returns to the Hollywood Bowl on June 25, 2027, with the show starting at 7:30 p.m.

The venue’s official event listing confirms a fourth year for the concert celebrating Hip-Hop history. General tickets go on sale November 13 at 10 a.m., following a November 12 presale at the same hour.

For now, The Roots are the only performers named on the 2027 event page. The date is locked into the calendar, but the listing doesn’t yet reveal which guests will join them.

That leaves room for another lineup built around the kind of cross-generational performances that brought the picnic west. The inaugural 2024 Hollywood Bowl edition featured Queen Latifah, Common, Digable Planets, Arrested Development, The Pharcyde and Black Sheep.

The following summer brought the Class of ’95 edition to the same venue on June 8, 2025. Its anniversary focus put a particular year in rap history at the center of the gathering.

Meanwhile, the Philadelphia event has kept building its own moments alongside the Los Angeles concerts. This year’s hometown festival booked Jay-Z for a performance with The Roots as he marked 30 years of Reasonable Doubt.

The 2027 Bowl listing also places the picnic in its Special Concerts series alongside opening night, Taskmaster and the July Fourth fireworks shows. Subscribers can access designated presales, while the venue’s Create Your Own option bundles three or more concerts with reduced ticket fees.

The Hollywood Bowl lists all ticket sales as final and notes that programs, artists, dates, prices and availability can change.

item.title: Mac Honors His Mother With Son Of Sheila As No Limit Tour Rolls On
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mac discussed his Son of Sheila tribute to his mother and the Cash Money-No Limit tour in a new 92Q interview with Silkk.
item.content:encoded:
Mac is putting his mother at the center of his next project, Son of Sheila (SOS), while revisiting the New Orleans history behind the Cash Money-No Limit tour. The rapper discussed the tribute during a new 92Q interview alongside Silkk The Shocker.

In the station’s account of its Rap Attack Official conversation, Mac and Silkk credited the labels’ Verzuz collaboration with helping set the tour in motion. Mac also said he imagined that kind of reunion while he was incarcerated, years before it became a touring reality.

Family has long been part of how Mac tells his story. In his ACLU biography, he recalled growing up with five siblings and spending time at their grandmother’s home in Uptown New Orleans.

Mac said in that earlier account: “Our parents always showed us love. We didn’t have much growing up, but we had love.” His family tribute arrives after a return to music that followed his June 2021 release from prison, where he spent 21 years.

Mac previously discussed that return and his album Son of the City during a February 2023 appearance on The Daily Show. The interview addressed his songwriting, the use of rap lyrics in court and his decision not to become bitter about his past.

His recording history reaches back much further than No Limit: Mac released Lyrical Midget at 12, with production from Mannie Fresh and Gregory D. He later joined Master P’s roster, releasing Shell Shocked in 1998 and following it with World War III. Shell Shocked reached No. 11 on the Billboard 200, according to his ACLU biography.

The 92Q conversation also covered the unexpected second life of I Can Tell on TikTok.

Mac recalled considering the record album filler, a sharp contrast with the attention it has received from listeners discovering it years later.

Since coming home, Mac has also worked with the Youth Empowerment Project to mentor young people. His ACLU biography describes that effort alongside his plans to keep recording and sharing his experiences.

Silkk also revisited his Mýa collaboration during the 92Q interview, recalling that he heard its potential immediately in the studio.

item.title: Flo Rida Headlines Miami Gala Targeting $5 Million For People With Intellectual Disabilities
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Flo Rida headlines a Miami fundraiser as Best Buddies aims to raise $5 million through its gala and cycling event.
item.content:encoded:
Flo Rida will bring his live show to a Miami fundraiser supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities this weekend.

He headlines the 28th annual Jersey Mike’s Subs Best Buddies Miami Gala on November 14 at Mana Wynwood.

Best Buddies International announced that the gala and its companion cycling event are expected to raise $5 million combined. The money supports programs covering employment, friendships, leadership training, inclusive living and family support.

Best Buddies founder Anthony K. Shriver connected the upcoming celebration to the nonprofit’s long-running community work.

“For nearly three decades, this event has brought our community together to create meaningful opportunities for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.”

The rapper has helped bring a crowd to this particular stage before. Best Buddies documented his performance at its 2018 Miami gala, when nearly 700 guests attended the Mana Wynwood event.

That earlier fundraiser collected $2.8 million, according to the organization’s account of the evening.

His connection to South Florida also runs through his business ventures beyond music. As AllHipHop previously reported, Flo Rida became an equity partner in Beyond Juicery + Eatery as the company looked to expand into the region.

This year’s gala has room for 850 guests, with cocktails and the silent auction beginning at 7 P.M. Dinner follows at 8:30 P.M., before organizers announce their Champion of the Year at 9:30 P.M.

That competition pairs community leaders with Best Buddies participants, with the top fundraising duo taking the title.

The weekend kicks off Friday with the inaugural Best Buddies Golf Classic at Turnberry Isle. Saturday morning brings a cycling challenge limited to 55 riders, with routes covering either 75 or 100 miles.

Chris Froome is among the professional cyclists joining the ride before attention turns to the evening fundraiser.

The official gala page lists an auction lineup featuring vacations, artwork and sporting experiences for supporters bidding throughout the night. Individual tickets are no longer available, although the event page directs supporters toward sponsorship and donation options.

Flo Rida is scheduled to take the stage Saturday at 10:30 P.M., with the evening ending at 11 P.M.

item.title: Summer Walker Faces LVRN Counterclaim Over Tour Money & Royalties
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Summer Walker's label demands tour proceeds and royalty payments as her bid to escape LVRN turns into a two-way legal fight.
item.content:encoded:
Summer Walker‘s fight to leave LVRN now carries a new financial threat from the company she says mishandled her money.

The Atlanta label is pursuing its own breach-of-contract counterclaim while denying her accusations of fraud.

LVRN says Walker owes money from three income streams, according to a new Fulton County filing obtained and first reported by Rolling Stone.

Its claims include 15 percent of income from business opportunities it secured and 20 percent of her songwriting performance royalties.

The company also alleges Walker stopped paying its seven percent share of her 2026 Finally Over It tour proceeds after initially making those payments. It’s asking for damages to be decided at trial and dismissal of her original complaint.

“At no time has LVRN acted in bad faith, been stubbornly litigious, or caused Walker unnecessary trouble and expense,” the company says in the filing.

Walker’s attorney Keith Moten hadn’t responded to the outlet’s request for comment when Wednesday’s report appeared.

Those demands answer a case Walker brought in August over an agreement she signed in September 2017.

Her original lawsuit accused LVRN of diverting money earmarked for touring, recordings, marketing and merchandise, while concealing financial information from her.

Walker also alleged she received no money from merchandise sold through Amazon or a YouTube page using her name and likeness. She’s seeking damages and a ruling ending the agreement, making the company’s control over her career part of the dispute alongside the accounting.

LVRN’s wider business now distributes through The Orchard, although its Interscope partnerships still include both Walker and fellow singer 6lack.

Her separate fight with Interscope involves an attempt to leave her recording agreement under California’s seven-year rule.

Interscope sued in October seeking at least $50 million over recordings it says she still owes, while Walker disputes those claims.

The company’s position is that her deal requires five studio albums, with Last Day of Summer and CLEAR excluded as earlier projects. Walker’s catalog under the labels includes Over It, Still Over It and Finally Over It.

A hearing in the separate Los Angeles Interscope case is scheduled for April 15.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Turns His Tattoos Into Chipotle Bags For Pittsburgh
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiz Khalifa puts Pittsburgh first with tattoo-inspired Chipotle bags, a one-hour giveaway and a separate national sweepstakes.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa is sending his own tattoos home with Pittsburgh customers through a limited Chipotle collaboration arriving Friday. He co-designed signed takeout bags inspired by his ink, putting his artwork into a promotion built around tattoo culture.

“I’ve been a big Chipotle fan for years, so seeing my tattoos take over the bags is wild,” Wiz Khalifa said. “Usually people are trying to get tatted like a Chipotle bag—now the Chipotle bags are tatted like me. Getting to do it in Pittsburgh makes it even better.”

The bags arrive November 13 at the restaurant’s 3510 Forbes Avenue location in Pittsburgh’s Oakland neighborhood.

The in-store giveaway runs from 3 to 4 P.M. Eastern, requires a purchase and limits it to one bag per person while supplies last. Meanwhile, participating U.S. and Canadian restaurants are offering tattooed customers buy-one-get-one entrees during that same hour in their respective time zones.

Temporary tattoos and drawn-on designs count alongside permanent ink, so customers don’t need a tattoo appointment to qualify.

The food offer requires an entree purchase of equal or greater value and doesn’t cover delivery, online orders or kids’ meals. Wiz’s double-chicken bowl with white rice, corn salsa and lettuce also joins the digital menu, with chips and guacamole on the side.

For people outside Pittsburgh, the official sweepstakes rules offer another way to win one of 13 bags without traveling. Eligible U.S. residents ages 13 and older need a Chipotle Rewards account, and minors also need permission from a parent or guardian. The rules value each bag at $5, with no cash alternative offered to the eventual winners.

The entry window opens November 12 and closes November 14, with ten rewards points buying one entry through the Rewards Exchange.

There’s also a mail-in option that doesn’t require redeeming points, and the combined limit is 20 entries per person. Mailed entries must be postmarked by November 14 and arrive by November 20.

The collaboration adds food packaging to a business portfolio already connected to Wiz’s personal tastes. AllHipHop previously covered Khalifa Kush’s planned New York expansion, which called for 36 dispensaries and an October 31 launch. That rollout involved flower and pre-rolls produced and distributed by Skyworld.

The sweepstakes drawing is scheduled for around November 21, and potential winners will be contacted through their account email.
